title: Mockup review — what changed
subtitle: Every screen touched by the review of Mockup_Review_Actions.md, before and after. Reference codes are the original comment ids (C…, S…, N…) from the action list.

screens.name: Sign up
notes: The mobile number is validated with a six-digit code. The email address is collected and never verified — nobody is locked out of a farm because an address bounced.
Signing in afterwards still accepts either one. It is registration that needs a proved number, because that is what work, alerts and a worker record are addressed to.
The old "type either one first and we ask for the other" behaviour has gone; the number is always the number field.

screens.name: Verify code
notes: The code always goes to the mobile number. An unverified address is never a route into the account.

screens.name: Your details and units
notes: Acre removed from the land measurement options, here and everywhere else in the app. Dunum and hectare only.

screens.name: Add your first farm
notes: "Draw my plots myself" is now "Draw my own plots".
Each route says WHEN to choose it. The two are not a beginner and an expert version; they answer different questions, and picking the wrong one changes what gets paid for.
The survey route states that plots can still be taken out of the result afterwards.
The satellite strip above the fork has gone — the coverage question replaces it.

screens.name: What should we cover?
notes: A new question, asked BEFORE the survey rather than after it: crops, trees, or both. It filters the survey result and both plan pages, so a date grower is not quoted for two hundred hectares of fallow ground.
The farm-name confirmation screen is gone entirely. Farms are named automatically and renamed at any time in Farm settings.
"What is growing here" is no longer asked of anyone. The survey detects it, and a question whose answer we already hold is a chance for the farmer to be wrong.

screens.name: Draw my own plots
notes: The crop picker under the canvas has gone.
The farmer names each plot instead. Left blank, it is numbered.
Plots already traced are listed, renameable and removable without leaving the screen. Before, a plot drawn round the wrong field could only be fixed by restarting the flow.

screens.name: Survey my whole farm
notes: "Send for survey" is now "Send for quote" — the survey is how it is done; the quote is what the farmer is waiting for.
The farm-name field has gone. The automatic name is stated instead, with where to change it.
One unit, not two: the bracketed second figure is gone from every area in the app, and hectares carry one decimal rather than two.

screens.name: What we found
notes: Structures are gone from the survey entirely — not excluded by default, removed. Reading buildings off imagery is a government-level service, not a farm one.
The name reads on the left and the actions sit on the right: Keep, Remove, Edit.
Remove greys the row rather than deleting it, and Keep puts it straight back.
The five edits are a four-tool toolbar on one line — Join, Split, Remove, Add — and choosing a tool asks which plots it applies to.
The "left out" total and the note about keeping a record of removed ground are both gone.
Confirm and continue moved into the totals box, so it arrives when the farmer has reached the end of the list.
A trees-only farm gets a count and a choice of tree type instead of a plot-by-plot menu.
Plots carry the names they will keep: the farm's name and a number.
No price on this screen. Pricing follows a confirmed scope and never runs beside one.

screens.name: Your plan and price
notes: The 30-day free trial leads the page instead of sitting in grey type under the fold.
"Compare all features" moved to the top — below two price cards nobody who had not already decided ever reached it.
Both Choose buttons are the same neutral colour, and the "Most chosen" badge has gone.
The annual option and its 15% discount are on each card, as a discount off the monthly figure rather than a second headline price.
Permission is asked for before any payment is taken, and the page says so.
The warnings are one group at the end under "Before you buy", not scattered through the page.

screens.name: Home
notes: The "All farms" tab is now "All plots", which is what it lists. Against "By farm" it was one word apart and described the same nouns.
Plot names are farm-qualified in this cross-farm list — Al Kharj North P1 — so a plot name means something out of context.

screens.name: Farm detail
notes: Three metrics, not four: Plant health, Water stress, Nutrition status.
Water stress is second — in this region it is the one that kills a crop inside a week.
"Growth and vigour" removed: it is an aspect of plant health rather than a thing beside it. The measure itself is untouched on the plot page and the map.
The "imagery from 2 August" line removed. How old the picture is stays on the farm card and on the plot's date stepper, beside the image it describes.

screens.name: Plots
notes: A legend at the top saying what the colours mean, built from the status scale so it cannot disagree with the rows under it.
A plot in trouble carries a direct route to the advice that says what to do, rather than making the farmer find it two screens away.
Farm-qualified plot names in the all-farms view; the short form inside one farm.

screens.name: Plot detail
notes: The measures, the date stepper and the explanatory content are unchanged — approved as they were.

The three values the watering calculation consumes — efficiency, soil, flow rate — are now editable here, from Edit on "This plot". They moved off the advice screens: they are properties of the plot, and they outlive any one recommendation.

screens.name: Crop cycles
notes: Where the satellite reads a different crop from the one entered, both answers are shown with the two dispositions that exist: "Update with satellite data" and "Keep as is".
The harvest date is ours now, and marked as an estimate rather than presented as a fact somebody typed.
No crop name in any plot name — a seasonal plot would need renaming every season.

screens.name: Add / edit crop cycle
notes: The expected harvest date field is gone. It was a guess typed in February about a date in November, never revisited.
"Sowing or planting date" is now "Planting date" — the two words describe the same moment for a farmer.
The crop and the planting date are the only things asked for.

screens.name: Tree list
notes: Filtering by tree type AND by variety. A grower asks at two levels — "show me the almonds" is a crop question, "show me the Khalas" is a variety one — and on a farm that is all date palm only the second answers anything.
Each filter appears only where the farm holds more than one of them.

screens.name: Tree detail
notes: "Chlorophyll" is now "Nutrient content". Chlorophyll is what the sensor measures; nutrition is what the farmer can act on, and colour words are not farmer language.
The upgrade copy behind it reads "Soil nutrient content".

screens.name: Add farm
notes: The warning threshold moved from five farms to ten, matching the hard limit. At five, a farmer with six was told twice he was near a limit he was nowhere near.
Route wording and when-to-use text match the first-run fork.

screens.name: Map
notes: The measure control is a bordered dropdown under a "Showing" label. It was a plain row with a small chevron on an unbordered panel, and reviewers did not discover that the whole measure list was behind it.

screens.name: Layers
notes: Two base maps, not three. Terrain was a third answer to a question with two real ones.
Each carries a description, because the difference that matters is clarity against freshness and the names do not say it.
Land use removed — it answers a planning question about somebody else's land.
Zoning removed — a reference to another platform's data model.
The irrigation map removed. What it was trying to show is the water stress map, which is already a measure layer, and the screen now says so.

Advanced map layers (soil type, testing labs) and Variable rate maps (sowing, nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium) removed in full, along with their feature keys and their lines in the plan comparison.

screens.name: Advice inbox
notes: Assign and Ignore, and nothing else. These are the two dispositions of a piece of advice.
"Mark as complete" is gone from the card. Completing work happens to a task, on a task screen; from here it closed an advice behind the back of the worker still holding the job.
Once the work has been sent the card points at the task rather than offering to assign one that already exists.
"Send them all to one person" turns every waiting item into work for one person, defaulting to the supervisor, and can be left standing.

screens.name: Irrigation advice
notes: The irrigation efficiency rating at the top, for this plot, showing only the level that applies.
One total, for the week. It used to print the weekly volume, then the volume per watering, then the same water as pump-hours, then again as litres per tree.
The recommendation stated as a change: "an increase of 20% on your usual watering". A raw volume means nothing to somebody who does not know what he usually applies.
A day and a time for each irrigation — the thing genuinely missing.
A two-hour window rather than a start time plus a duration: without a measured flow rate, "6 p.m. for 2 h 6 m" is a precision the app does not have.
One plot, one schedule, said on the screen. A per-tree schedule is not a thing that can be carried out.
Over- and under-watering feedback sits here, as an instruction to increase or reduce.
The Diagnosis section and the Assumptions section are both gone.

screens.name: Nutrition advice
notes: Diagnosis and Assumptions removed here too, not only on D2 — model inputs with their values are an agronomist's working, and this screen is read by the person loading the spreader.
Nothing is lost from the record: every input is still written to the advisory log before anyone sees the advice, and the log opens from the ⋯ menu.

screens.name: Crop protection advice
notes: Diagnosis removed. The active ingredient, the rate, the pre-harvest interval and the label warning — the things somebody about to spray needs — are untouched.

screens.name: Tasks
notes: The SUGGESTED section is gone. A task is an advice that has been assigned; assigning is the event that creates it, not a property set on one that already exists.
The Ignore button is off the task list with it.
The list now contains work that has actually been given to somebody, which is what makes "3 tasks today" a number a supervisor can trust.

screens.name: Task detail
notes: Mark as done is a task action and lives here.
For a task raised from advice it opens the advised-versus-applied record rather than the plain completion form, because that is the question worth asking about advice.

screens.name: Compare plans
notes: Basic and Pro are ROWS within each feature group, and Pro lists only what it adds. The old two-column table was mostly rows reading "yes | yes" — a feature list wearing a comparison's clothes.
Filtered to the service the account holds; the tabs appear only for an account holding both.
The same group order for crops and for trees, satellite and imagery first in both.
The "Upgrade" button is now "Choose a plan".

Seventeen renames: comparison maps, farm advisory, farm activity tracking, date palm variety identification, tree health status, soil nutrient content, automated alerts, task assignment, and the rest.
Ten removals: historical weather, time series, expert opinion, Agro Doctor, guaranteed reports, photosynthesis, stress detection, chlorophyll, fruit tree health.
Multi-user access and the five languages moved into "In every plan" — listing them per tier put two ticks beside each and implied a difference that is not there.

screens.name: Language and region
notes: Acres removed from the area units.
A 24-hour / a.m.–p.m. setting, because the irrigation plan prints a time window on every watering.

screens.name: Choose a measure
notes: Each measure is its own block with room around it. It was a title, a technical name and a full sentence of explanation crushed into a 48 dp row, six times over — the densest thing in the app, on the screen a farmer uses to decide what he is looking at.

screens.name: Plot tool picker — new
notes: Choosing a tool on A11 asks which plots it applies to. Before, joining meant discovering that tapping a second row while a first was selected silently built a set — a gesture nobody performs by accident and therefore nobody performed at all.

screens.name: Send them all to one person — new
notes: Every waiting piece of advice becomes a task for one person, due when the app suggested.
The supervisor is offered first and pre-selected, because that is who the farmer picks by hand every time.
"Keep doing this" makes it standing. It is deliberately not silent: what went out and to whom stays visible, and it can be switched off from the same line.

screens.name: How we calculate for this plot
notes: This used to open from an "Assumptions we used" block on every advice screen, keyed by advice.
It now opens from the plot's own record on B4, keyed by plot — which is what efficiency, soil and flow rate actually belong to. They outlive any one recommendation and they change every future one.
